title: B2+ · L10 — Crisis communication
description: Comunicar en crisis: tono calmado, factual, responsable. Manejar outages, PR issues, y escalaciones a stakeholders.

questions.prompt: Producto down desde hace 12 minutos. Miles de usuarios afectados. Tienes que publicar el primer update en status page.
questions.question: Your service is down. Which is the strongest first update to customers?
options: We're aware of an incident affecting X, we're actively investigating, and we'll update every 15 minutes.
questions.explanation: Formula estandar de crisis comms tech (SRE / DevOps playbook): AWARENESS (sabemos) + SCOPE (que afecta) + ACTION (estamos investigando) + CADENCE (cuando actualizamos). La cadencia comprometida es la parte mas critica — reduce el pico de tickets/tweets del 60-70% porque los usuarios ya no sienten necesidad de contactar. 'Something broke' o 'unknown issue' aumentan panic. Registro pro: 'incident' es el termino tecnico correcto (no 'problem' ni 'issue' — 'incident' comunica gravedad calibrada y proceso formal en curso).
examples: We're aware of intermittent errors on login. Investigating. Next update at 14:00 UTC. → status page tipico
Incident in progress affecting the API. On it. Updates every 30 minutes. → registro conciso pro

questions.prompt: Cliente enterprise ha perdido 4 horas de trabajo por vuestro outage. Reunion de post-crisis con su CTO.
questions.question: Which crisis message avoids the WORST mistake?
options: We take full accountability for the impact this has had on your teams.
questions.explanation: 'We take full accountability' es LA formula de crisis pro, mantra de comunicacion moderna post-crisis (Boeing 737 MAX crisis mostro el precio de no decirla). NUNCA deflectar culpa publicamente — aunque un vendor haya fallado, publicamente asumes ownership porque el cliente contrato contigo, no con tu vendor. 'Impact on your teams' centra al cliente afectado, no a tu empresa (empathy focus). Error hispano cultural: la instinctividad de defenderse por reputacion; en anglo corporate la mejor defensa es la accountability radical.
examples: We own this fully — this is on us. Here's what we're doing about it. → US register directo
Full accountability. Here's what happened and here's what we're doing to make it right. → estructura pro

questions.statement: In a crisis, saying 'no comment' is generally the safest option.
questions.explanation: FALSO — 'no comment' es la peor jugada en la mayoria de crisis modernas. En la percepcion publica y periodistica, 'no comment' se interpreta como admision implicita de culpa o de que hay algo que esconder. El silencio de la empresa se llena con rumores, hilos de Twitter especulativos, y narrativas de terceros. La mejor defensa: comunicacion factual controlada, frecuente, con lo que SI puedes decir con confianza. Registro anti-crisis PR: 'Here's what we know now, here's what we're doing, next update at X'.
examples: Weak: We have no comment at this time. → invita especulacion
Strong: Here's what we know now, here's what we're doing, next update at 5 PM. → controla la narrativa

questions.prompt: Escribes el segundo update de crisis 30 minutos despues del inicial. Que debe contener obligatoriamente?
questions.question: Which is the best structure for a crisis update?
options: What happened + Impact + What we're doing + When you'll hear from us next.
questions.explanation: Estructura canonica de crisis update (Atlassian / PagerDuty playbook): (1) hechos verificados, (2) impacto especifico, (3) accion en curso, (4) cadence del proximo update. El punto #4 es el mas critico y mas olvidado — los stakeholders necesitan CERTIDUMBRE sobre cuando volveras a hablar, incluso si es 'no news yet'. Regla: SIEMPRE termina con timestamp del proximo update. Error hispano: dar contexto largo y olvidar la cadence — dispara ansiedad y tickets al soporte.
examples: Incident update: [What] [Impact] [Action] [Next update time]. → template textbook
Same format every 30 min — even if nothing has changed. → disciplina de cadence

questions.text: We deeply regret the disruption this has caused, and we're doing everything in our power to restore service.
questions.explanation: Formula de disculpa corporativa formal. Fenomeno de connected speech: 'deeply regret' con doble /r/ pero enlazado /diːpliriˈɡret/; 'in our power' con weak form /ɪnaʊəˈpaʊə/; 'to restore' con weak /təriˈstɔː/. Colocaciones nativas del registro corporate: 'deeply regret' (mas formal que 'sorry'), 'in our power' (dentro de nuestras posibilidades — colocacion pulida), 'restore service' (restablecer — verbo tecnico obligatorio, no 'fix'). Registro: 'sorry' es demasiado informal en comms corporativos serios.
examples: We sincerely apologize for the disruption to your operations. → alternativa formal
We deeply regret the impact and are working around the clock to resolve it. → 'around the clock' = 24/7

questions.prompt: Han pasado 45 minutos y no sabes que causo el outage. Los stakeholders piden respuestas.
questions.question: You're unsure of the cause. Which is best?
options: We're actively investigating the root cause and will share findings as soon as we've confirmed them.
questions.explanation: 'Actively investigating' + 'as soon as we've confirmed them' comunica accion sin especular. LA regla de oro de crisis comms: NUNCA especular. Especular en crisis puede empeorar dramaticamente la situacion si la hipotesis inicial resulta incorrecta (perdes credibilidad doble: por el fallo y por la mala info). 'Root cause' es el termino tecnico universal en incident management (no 'cause of the problem'). Registro: 'active' + 'confirmed' comunica proceso serio, no improvisacion.
examples: Investigation ongoing — we'll share verified findings, not speculation. → transparencia adulta
Root cause TBC. Will update once confirmed by the eng team. → 'TBC' = to be confirmed (jerga)

questions.prompt: Empareja cada termino de incident/crisis management con su traduccion:
questions.explanation: Seis terminos indispensables del vocabulario SRE/DevOps de incident management. 'Post-mortem' (latin: 'despues de la muerte') = analisis retrospectivo del incidente, cultura estandar en tech: aprender del fallo sin culpar personas (blameless). 'Root cause' vs 'immediate cause' — importante distincion: lo que dispara el fallo vs lo que lo hace posible. 'Mitigation' (paliativo temporal) vs 'fix' (solucion permanente). 'Downtime' se cuantifica en 'nines' (99.9%, 99.99%).
examples: We'll publish a full post-mortem within 48 hours, including timeline and prevention plan.
Downtime was 47 minutes; root cause identified, mitigation deployed, permanent fix in progress. → estructura pro

questions.target: This shouldn't have happened, and we owe you a clear explanation of what went wrong and how we'll prevent it going forward.
questions.explanation: Comunicacion de crisis nivel CEO/VP para stakeholders enterprise. Triple estructura: reconocimiento del error ('shouldn't have happened'), commitment con transparencia ('owe you a clear explanation'), forward-looking ('prevent going forward'). 'Owe you' es lenguaje potente — implica deuda moral, no favor. Ritmo natural: tono firme y bajo, sin acelerar, pausas marcadas tras 'happened,' y 'wrong'. Contracciones: 'shouldn't', 'we'll' obligatorias en spoken. Este mensaje se ha usado literalmente por CEOs post-outage.
examples: This is unacceptable and we owe you better. Here's our plan going forward.
You deserve transparency on what failed and how we're fixing it. Here it is. → 'deserve' potente

questions.prompt: Vuestro cloud provider tuvo un fallo que os afecto. Que NO debes hacer en comms publicos?
questions.question: Which does NOT belong in crisis communication?
questions.explanation: Culpar publicamente a terceros (aunque sea verdad) destruye credibilidad y proyecta debilidad. Aunque tu vendor haya fallado literalmente, el cliente te contrato a TI — publicamente asumes ownership, y en privado gestionas con el vendor. Empresas que culpan publicamente a AWS/Google Cloud durante outages son juzgadas negativamente por su lack de fallback design. Registro: internamente puedes decir 'AWS caused this'; externamente 'we depend on X and we should have had a fallback'. Ownership radical = cultura fuerte.
examples: Weak: Our cloud provider had an outage — nothing we could do. → deflection publico
Strong: We depend on X; we should have had a fallback. We're building one now. → ownership pro

questions.statement: In crisis, overcommunicating is better than undercommunicating.
questions.explanation: VERDADERO — es la REGLA #1 de crisis comms moderna. Cadencia frecuente supera precision perfecta. Un update 'nothing new to report' cada 30 min es MEJOR que silencio de 2 horas seguido de un update completo. Razon psicologica: el silencio dispara ansiedad exponencialmente; los updates regulares (aun sin novedad) transmiten control. Studios de PR en crisis (Toyota, BP, Boeing) muestran que la cadencia de comunicacion predice mejor la recuperacion de confianza que la calidad del contenido del update.
examples: Update: Still investigating. No new info. Next update in 30 min. → cadence sin sustancia = ok
Standing by. Team on it. Will share the moment we know more. → holding statement pro

questions.prompt: Rueda de prensa post-crisis. Un periodista te lanza una pregunta hostil buscando titulares.
questions.question: The press/customer asks a hostile question. Which is best?
options: That's a fair question, and one we're asking ourselves. Here's what we know so far.
questions.explanation: Tecnica de spokesperson entrenado. 'Fair question' DESARMA la hostilidad (validas la legitimidad de preguntar), 'one we're asking ourselves' muestra que reflexionas internamente (no complacencia), 'here's what we know' es el 'bridging' clasico al mensaje que preparaste (siempre pivotas al terreno que dominas). Nunca insultar la pregunta ('stupid') — el titular sera sobre tu insulto, no sobre la respuesta. 'No comment' invita al drama. Colocacion nativa: 'here's what we know so far' es formula magica de spokesperson.
examples: It's a fair question, and we're actively investigating. Here's what I can confirm today. → bridge pulido
Legitimate concern — here's what we can share with confidence today. → deflect + pivot

questions.text: As of now, service has been fully restored, and we're monitoring closely to ensure stability over the next twenty-four hours.
questions.explanation: Cierre estandar post-incidente. Fenomeno de connected speech: 'as of now' con /zə/ /ˈæzəvnaʊ/; 'fully restored' con /liː-riː/ enlazado; 'twenty-four' se pronuncia como una unidad rapida /ˈtwentiˈfɔː/. Colocaciones nativas: 'as of now' (a partir de ahora — presente perfecto sujeto a cambio), 'fully restored' (restablecido totalmente), 'monitoring closely' (monitoreando de cerca), 'over the next X hours' (durante las proximas X horas). Comunicacion adulta y honesta: promete continuar vigilando.
examples: Service is back. Watching closely for the next 24 hours. → registro casual pro
Restored as of 15:42 UTC. Extended monitoring in place through EOD. → registro formal preciso

questions.prompt: Detectas un P0 (production down) a las 14:03. Necesitas escalar en Slack #incidents inmediatamente.
questions.question: Which internal escalation message is strongest?
options: P0 incident: production auth service down since 14:03. Impact: all logins failing. Bridge open: [link]. IC: Priya. Need: comms sign-off.
questions.explanation: Formato senior de incident escalation en engineering culture moderna. Estructura pentagonal: (1) SEVERIDAD con nomenclatura estandar (P0/P1/SEV1), (2) SERVICIO afectado + timestamp exacto, (3) IMPACTO cuantificado, (4) BRIDGE (link a Zoom/Slack huddle activo), (5) IC (Incident Commander asignado) + SPECIFIC ASK. Reduce friccion a segundos para que el respondedor sepa que hacer. 'Emergency!' o 'help now' generan panic sin actionability. Registro: jerga standard en tech companies (Google, Netflix, Stripe usan variantes de este formato).
examples: P1: checkout down since 09:14. Bridge: [link]. IC: Marcus. Need: SRE support. → formato pentagonal
SEV2: payments latency spike. Impacted: 12% of users. IC: on-call. Need: exec awareness. → escalada calibrada

questions.statement: 'Blameless post-mortem' means no one is held accountable for mistakes.
questions.explanation: FALSO — malinterpretacion frecuente. 'Blameless' significa: no CULPAR a personas por errores humanos individuales, PORQUE los errores humanos son sintomas de fallos SISTEMICOS que hay que arreglar. Pero se identifican fallas del sistema, se documentan aprendizajes, y se implementan changes. Accountability existe a nivel de equipo/sistema; personal blame no. Cultura moderna DevOps (Google SRE book, Etsy, Netflix). Diferencia critica: 'blameless' ≠ 'careless'. Los equipos blameless suelen tener MAS accountability, no menos.
examples: Blameless doesn't mean careless — we still hold ourselves to the highest standards. → clarifica confusion
We look at systems, not people. But we ship the fix and own the learnings. → doble commitment

questions.target: We know trust takes years to build and seconds to lose. Here's exactly what happened, and here's how we'll earn back your confidence.
questions.explanation: Cierre de crisis nivel CEO — clasico del genero. 'Trust takes years to build and seconds to lose' es aforismo corporativo tan usado que raya en cliche pero funciona (Buffett lo hizo famoso). Estructura triple: reconocimiento del dano ('lose') + transparencia ('exactly what happened') + commitment futuro ('earn back your confidence'). Ritmo natural: tono suave y bajo, pausas marcadas, sin defensividad. Contracciones: 'we'll' obligatoria. Este cierre se ha usado literalmente en cartas de disculpa de Airbnb, Uber, Facebook post-crisis.
examples: We've let you down. Here's our commitment to earning your trust back. → registro directo
Trust is hard-won and easily lost. Here's our plan to rebuild it, step by step. → registro reflexivo
